# PR #149 round 6 correctness review

## A) Verdict

**PASS-WITH-NOTES** at `5963c27c9957bfd97cdaf84092493a44dd6fdbb1`.

**F005 and N001 closed.** The earlier F001-F004 closures stand.

## B) Scope and proof

Reviewed only `e0004f856f665cdeec03a62b0f48e769f342bea2..5963c27c9957bfd97cdaf84092493a44dd6fdbb1`: e06b5438's repair and the main merge/migration renumber. Previously reviewed main imports are not a new full-plan review.

Clean pinned checkout; GitHub and ls-remote agree, CLEAN. Latest checks succeeded, including the delivers run superseding its cancelled predecessor. CI `42390381816`, attempt 1, is at this exact head: 2,122 JUnit cases, zero failures/errors. No local builds/tests, mutations, shell probes, captures or live measurements.

## C) F005 closed: stored intent, fixed sender

Both first-close and owed-retry call notify_owned with only the recorded ClosedRoleRequest. The retrier's actor and reason cannot enter the notice construction. The one notice Msg is from pij-bg, to the recorded requester, with the original closed_by, close_bound and close_why; pane-bound versus asserted identity is labelled in the body.

close_bound is captured from the resolved caller and stored alongside the move/delete and request.closed_by_actor audit in the same owned transaction. Retry still checks authority to trigger the stored intent but neither rewrites it nor publishes a new closer assertion. The successful retry line explicitly says its supplied --why is not used.

The executed close regression verifies an asserted holder triggers D's owed notice, whose sender is pij-bg and body retains D's binding/reason, not the retrier's reason. The row becomes told; another close sends nothing. A requester-triggered owed retry succeeds and admits one more FYI without self-addressing.

The notice task remains independently owned after admission. Its stable request-closed message id and sender preserve FYI deduplication; marking told happens only after hold_fyi succeeds. Quiet/requester first-close still owes nothing.

## D) N001 closed

render_holdings now prints `window unchanged: <reason>` even when the safe failure receipt has name:null. The executed CLI control checks the failed holdings lookup appears in the release line. The existing protection against renaming on a failed read remains.

## E) Merge and earlier guards

The owned role drain/gate file is byte-unchanged from e0004f8. Its cancelled-assign continuation and retirement-waits-for-delivery controls both executed in the new CI run. Caller binding still refuses contradictory pane/id input; asserted-only authority remains requester/holder, not PA/prime.

Migration 0037 is renamed 0040, with close_bound retained; SCHEMA_VERSION and user_version are 40. The API reference follows the renumber. Main's 0039 imports are retained.

## F) C32 boundary

The inspected request-close notice path has one Msg construction, with the fixed daemon sender. It replays the stored initial intent rather than acting as the retrier; the initial mutation and actor audit remain atomic. The Known limit explicitly names PRD 003 req-10 and discloses asserted requester/holder close/withdraw authority.

This closes the correctness-side sender/replay defects. Herring owns the independent four-condition C32 security verdict; this is not a claim that caller provenance itself is solved.

## G) Notes

The owed-notice test seeds a closed owed row, including binding but no audit event. It proves replay/requester recovery and repeat suppression, not an end-to-end notification-failure or cancellation reproduction. Transaction/task ownership is source-reviewed; no reviewer mutation is claimed.

No new per-tick work was added. Live cost proof remains performance-owned. #156 also has unmerged migration 0040: the later merger must renumber and obtain fresh exact-head evidence. Already-applied private prototypes are not automatically checksum-upgraded.

## H) Handover

No further correctness repair requested for this delta. Preserve the replay and human-error controls; keep C32 acceptance and merge-order migration numbering with their owners. No product code was changed by this reviewer.
